MAIN APPEAL

The appellant-State State of Punjab, by instituting the present appeal preferred under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 Act") seeks setting aside of the award dated (for short "1894 Act"), 28.10.1997 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Patiala (hereinafter to be referred as "Reference Court") while restoring the Award passed by the Land Acquisition Collector Collector, SYL, Patiala (for short "LAC").

"LAC") 1 of 4 [2] Briefly, the facts are that in pursuance of Punjab Govt. Notification under Sections 4 & 6 of the 1894 Act issued on 24.09.1987 & 13.10.1987 respectively,
certain land of the respondents-landowners, situated within the revenue estate of Village Gajdi Nagar, Tehsil Rajpura, District Patiala, was acquired.
The acquisition was made for public purpose, namely, "for construction of Banur Distributory".
The LAC, vide Award No. 281/P-SYL, dated 16.05.1988, assessed market value at the rate of Rs.60,000/- per acre for the Chahi land, while Rs. 35,000/- per acre was given for Gair Mumkin land.

Besides it, vide supplementary award No. 392/P/SYL, dated 23.10.1989, the LAC awarded 20% of the market value as severance compensation for State Of Punjab vs Parveen Kuamr And Ors on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40574234/

sentences.text: [ 3 ] Dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award, landowners / interested persons filed objections under Section 18 of the Act of 1894, which were partly allowed vide decision dated 28.10.1997 by the learned Reference Court, whereby the market value of the acquired land was assessed / enhanced at the rate of Rs. 27,200/- per bigha for Chahi land, whereas Rs. 9,600/- per bigha was granted for Gair Mumkin land.

The learned Reference Court also granted compensation for severance at the rate of 20%
of the market value for the un-acquired land located beyond the distributory, whereas for the unacquired land measuring 40 bighas 11 biswas on the village side of the distributory, the compensation on account of severance was granted at the rate of 15% of the market value of the acquired land, subject to a maximum of 5 acres.
2 of 4
[4] Being dissatisfied with the determination made by the learned Reference Court, the appellant-State of Punjab is in the present appeal.
[5] No one has chosen to appear on behalf of the respondents-landowners.
[6] I have heard learned counsel for the appellant and gone through the paper-book/relevant record.

[7] With respect to the market value awarded by the learned Reference Court, no interference is called for as the same is based on proper appreciation of evidence and nothing material has been left for consideration.

A perusal of the judgment passed by the learned Reference Court shows that reliance was placed upon a previous Reference Court's award dated 02.12.1991 (Ex.P-2) pertaining to the same notification /acquisition proceedings carried out in the same village, regarding which the same Award was passed by the LAC on 16.05.1988, whereby the market value of the Chahi land and Gair Mumkin land was assessed @ Rs.27,200/- & Rs. 9,600/- per bigha respectively, the respondents-landowners were also awarded the same compensation.
Furthermore, considering the fact the land in the present case was acquired for the public purpose, namely," for construction of Banur Distributory" which definitely and conclusively dissected the land holdings into two parts, in such circumstances, the respondents/landowners definitely suffered loss towards cultivation of land besides inconvenience towards connectivity of the parcels left on either side of the Minor.
Moreover, severance also causes reduction in value of remaining land due to alteration in access, useability, 3 of 4 irregularity of shape and loss of agricultural viability etc.

No material evidence has been pointed out on behalf of the appellant-State of Punjab so as to show that the findings recorded by the learned Reference Court with respect to severance of land pertaining to the respondents-landowners are against the records.

In such circumstances, the damages towards severance of land as granted by the learned Reference Court ranging State Of Punjab vs Parveen Kuamr And Ors on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40574234/
2 between 15-20% of the compensation cannot be held to be illegal and unjustified.
